facts.claim: 作者把「冰人」这类物理/温度双关收进数学科学章：一个人由冰构成、体温低于零度，落点是他是个 ice guy（冰做的家伙）。
facts.quote: I’ve just met a man who appears to be made out of frozen water and has a core temperature of below 0 degrees Celsius.

facts.claim: 中子进酒吧的笑话把「不收费」与「不带电荷」压在同一句 No charge 上，让物理属性直接充当酒保台词。
facts.quote: A neutron goes into a bar and orders a drink. ‘How much do I owe you?’ it asks. ‘For you?’ says the barman, ‘No charge.’

facts.claim: 作者用「原子构成万物／原子凭空编造」的双关解释科学家为何不信原子，机制是 make up 的双义。
facts.quote: Why don’t scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything.

facts.claim: 负数笑话把习语 stop at nothing（不择手段）字面化为「停在 nothing 上」，于是怕负数的人恰好永远不碰负数。
facts.quote: Did you hear about the mathematician who’s afraid of negative numbers? He’ll stop at nothing to avoid them.

facts.claim: 光子登机笑话靠 travelling light 的双义（轻装旅行／以光速旅行）收尾，属于物理属性被塞进日常对白的一类。
facts.quote: ‘Do you have any luggage?’ says the person behind the desk. ‘No,’ says the photon, ‘I’m travelling light.’

facts.claim: 电子丢失笑话用 positive 的双义（确定／带正电）作结，把粒子电荷说成失物招领时的一句口头确认。
facts.quote: ‘Oh no, I think I lost an electron!’ ‘Are you sure?’ says the other. ‘Yep,’ says the first one, ‘I’m positive.’

facts.claim: 薛定谔的猫被改写成通缉犯 wanted dead and alive，把「既死又活」的叠加态直接搬进西部片通缉令的句式。
facts.quote: Schrödinger’s Cat recently went on a crime spree and is now wanted dead and alive.

facts.claim: 章末并入的「Jokes for mathematical geniuses」小节另收一批需要进阶数学背景的笑话（外推、分子/分母、斐波那契、函数进酒吧、八进制与十六进制），斐波那契那条把数列增长说成派对规模。
facts.quote: I’m looking forward to this year’s Fibonacci party. Apparently it’s as big as the last two put together.

relations.pair: “There are 10 types of people …” / “There are two types of people …”
relations.relation: 同一「世上有 N 种人」句式在正章与并入的数学天才小节各出现一次；后者把列表故意停在省略号上，用「数据不完整」自我指涉，是对前者的进阶改写。
relations.quote: There are two types of people in the world: those who can extrapolate information from incomplete data sets …

relations.pair: “Why was 6 afraid of 7?” / “Why was 49 afraid of 50?”
relations.relation: 两则是同一「数字名谐音成句」机制的两个变体：7 8 9 读作 seven ate nine，49 与 50 打架后 51 读作 fifty won。
relations.quote: Why was 49 afraid of 50? Because they had a fight, and 51.

relations.pair: “5 out of 4 people … fractions” / “numerators and denominators … only a fraction”
relations.relation: 两处都拿 fraction 的双义（分数／一小部分）做文章，前者用统计句式把比例说反，后者用分子分母之分说「只有一小部分人懂」。
relations.quote: Apparently 5 out of 4 people say they don’t use fractions properly.

relations.pair: “Stand in the corner, it’s 90 degrees!” / “put it in the oven at 180 degrees”
relations.relation: 两则共用「度数」一词，把几何角度与温度/烤箱设定互换，让听者先按一个义项理解、再被另一个义项纠正。
relations.quote: What should you do if you’re cold in a rectangular room? Stand in the corner, it’s 90 degrees!

numbers.meaning: 冰人笑话给出的核心体温，是「由冰构成」这一双关成立的物理前提。
numbers.quote: has a core temperature of below 0 degrees Celsius

numbers.meaning: 科学家看地球自转 24 小时后觉得无聊，于是 call it a day（收工／把这一天叫作一天）。
numbers.quote: Scientists reported getting bored after watching the Earth turn for 24 hours

numbers.meaning: 数学家按烤箱温度 180 度理解披萨盒说明，于是配料全掉了——角度单位被当成烘焙温度。
numbers.quote: The instructions said to put it in the oven at 180 degrees.

numbers.meaning: 二进制笑话里的 10 实际是十进制 2，所以「10 种人」的字面数量与真实类别数故意对不上。
numbers.quote: There are 10 types of people in the world: those that understand binary and those that don’t.

numbers.meaning: 程序员混淆万圣节与圣诞节，因为八进制 31 等于十进制 25，Oct/Dec 又恰好是十月/十二月的缩写。
numbers.quote: Why do computer programmers mix up Halloween and Christmas? Because Oct 31 = Dec 25.
